name: Ernst Röhm
role: Chief of staff of the Sturmabteilung
description: Nazi paramilitary leader assessed during his SA command, including political violence, military ambitions and the proposed continuation of the National Socialist revolution.

religion.reason: The reviewed political biographies do not firmly establish his personal religious identification during SA leadership.

sources.title: Röhm, Ernst
sources.publisher: Munich Documentation Centre for the History of National Socialism

sources.title: Gay men under the Nazi regime

axes.brief: Paramilitary revolutionary power and elimination of rival parties reject accountable popular competition.
axes.counterEvidence: Conflict with Hitler concerned SA power, not a programme for pluralist democracy.

axes.brief: SA intimidation and repression subordinate civil liberties to the national revolution.
axes.counterEvidence: Paramilitary firearms do not prove an equal civilian right; Nazi suppression of hatred was selective rather than viewpoint-neutral.

axes.brief: Nazi national and racial exclusion is incompatible with equal plural citizenship.
axes.counterEvidence: Individual fellowship inside the SA does not imply equal rights for excluded ethnic groups.

qualifications.15: The statement specifically includes several distinct ways of life within national identity; it does not ask whether a common national identity should exist.

axes.brief: Racial national membership restricts settlement and equal admission.
axes.counterEvidence: Military service abroad is not a general plural migration programme; exact visa tools remain analogies.

qualifications.5: The statement permits permanent refugee settlement regardless of skills or cultural compatibility. The answer concerns this unconditional clause, separately from selected humanitarian admissions.

axes.brief: Armed mobilisation and the projected SA people’s army prioritise militarised national strength.
axes.counterEvidence: The assessed period precedes the Second World War; later campaigns cannot be presented as his actions.

axes.brief: Rearmament and rejection of Versailles constraints privilege national freedom of action.
axes.counterEvidence: His earlier Bolivia contract is cross-border employment, not consent to supranational sovereignty.

axes.brief: The second revolution’s anti-capitalist direction makes strategic public control plausible.
axes.counterEvidence: The detailed nationalisation proposals are attributed to a broader radical faction; he did not supply a complete sector-by-sector ownership plan.

axes.brief: Revolutionary national strength and economic independence favour domestic strategic production.
axes.counterEvidence: This is a contextual programme estimate, not a documented personal customs schedule.

axes.brief: National mobilisation and radical economic change favour coordination over unrestricted capital allocation.
axes.counterEvidence: Anti-capitalist rhetoric and SA patronage do not establish the precise planning mechanisms of Marxist socialism.

axes.brief: Working-class SA mobilisation and hostility to established elites favour material improvement for national insiders.
axes.counterEvidence: Racial exclusion, personal patronage and military primacy sharply limit universal egalitarian interpretation.

axes.brief: Party and military authority rather than clergy directs the proposed political order.
axes.counterEvidence: No firm personal religious identification or comprehensive personal church-state programme is established.

axes.brief: Personal same-sex relationships coexist with nationalist masculine hierarchy and SA participation in repression.
axes.counterEvidence: His sexuality does not establish equal marriage, women’s equality or a general LGBT-rights programme.

axes.brief: Military modernisation and revolutionary transformation favour practical technical development.
axes.counterEvidence: No personal modern genetic or AI programme exists; caution is inferred where bodily and social effects conflict.

axes.brief: SA reorganisation centralised groups under Röhm rather than autonomous regional party oversight.
axes.counterEvidence: Seeking organisational autonomy from Hitler or the army is not decentralised public sovereignty.

axes.brief: Nazi racial heredity and conventional sex-role ideas coexist with militant training and political socialisation.
axes.counterEvidence: Specific causal shares for temperament and risk-taking are inferred, not documented biological claims by Röhm.
